newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 7.

text.p: There are 85 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that according to a recent report, Hong Kong young people were becoming more tolerant towards corruption. If Hong Kong wanted to continue to be a financial centre in Asia, it had to strengthen young people's sense of commercial integrity and law and maintain the freedom of expression, the paper said.

-- WEN WEI PO said that judging from a speech recently given by an army general, the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison had proved to be a civilised army, and its soldiers in Hong Kong would strictly abide by local laws. Hong Kong people had no reason to worry, the paper said.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said that unless modifications were made and the Special Administrative Region was given some say in the types of mainlanders coming in, the situation could get out of hand. At least half a million mainlanders would make their homes here if the present rate of entry remained unchanged, and that would affect Hong Kong people's way of life, which the Basic Law guaranteed would not be changed, the paper said.
